//! Every branching construct ADR 0036 names a Rust counting rule for, one
//! function per shape, so a complexity walk can be checked against a number
//! derived by hand in the README beside this file.

/// An `else if` chain: three `if_expression` nodes, the inner two nested in the
/// outer's `else` branch.
pub fn classify(n: i64) -> &'static str {
    if n < 0 {
        "negative"
    } else if n == 0 {
        "zero"
    } else if n < 10 {
        "small"
    } else {
        "large"
    }
}

/// One `if`, one `&&` and one `||`.
pub fn guarded(a: bool, b: bool, c: bool) -> i64 {
    if a && b || c {
        1
    } else {
        0
    }
}

/// `if let` — the same `if_expression` node as the boolean form, with a pattern
/// where the condition would be.
pub fn unwrap_or_zero(value: Option<i64>) -> i64 {
    if let Some(n) = value {
        n
    } else {
        0
    }
}

/// `while let`, likewise one `while_expression`.
pub fn drain(mut items: Vec<i64>) -> i64 {
    let mut total = 0;
    while let Some(n) = items.pop() {
        total += n;
    }
    total
}

/// A plain `while`.
pub fn countdown(mut n: i64) -> i64 {
    let mut steps = 0;
    while n > 0 {
        n -= 1;
        steps += 1;
    }
    steps
}

/// A `for`, with an `if` in its body.
pub fn first_even(items: &[i64]) -> Option<i64> {
    for item in items {
        if item % 2 == 0 {
            return Some(*item);
        }
    }
    None
}

/// An unconditional `loop`, which counts even though it branches nowhere by
/// itself — Go's `complexity()` counts a bare `for {}` the same way.
pub fn poll_until(limit: i64) -> i64 {
    let mut n = 0;
    loop {
        n += 1;
        if n >= limit {
            return n;
        }
    }
}

/// A `match` whose catch-all is the literal `_` wildcard, which does not count.
pub fn describe(n: i64) -> &'static str {
    match n {
        0 => "zero",
        1 => "one",
        2 => "two",
        _ => "many",
    }
}

/// A `match` whose catch-all is a binding, which does count: only the wildcard
/// token itself is treated as `default`.
pub fn label(n: i64) -> String {
    match n {
        0 => "zero".to_string(),
        other => format!("n={}", other),
    }
}

/// Two `?` operators, each the `if err != nil { return err }` a Go author
/// writes out.
pub fn parse_pair(text: &str) -> Result<(i64, i64), std::num::ParseIntError> {
    let mut parts = text.split(',');
    let first: i64 = parts.next().unwrap_or("0").trim().parse()?;
    let second: i64 = parts.next().unwrap_or("0").trim().parse()?;
    Ok((first, second))
}

/// A closure, whose branches count toward the function whose span contains it.
pub fn tally(items: &[i64]) -> i64 {
    let keep = |n: &&i64| **n > 0 && **n < 100;
    items.iter().filter(keep).copied().sum()
}

/// A nested `fn` item: scored as its own function, with its lines out of this
/// one's span and a flat +1 left behind here.
pub fn outer(n: i64) -> i64 {
    fn inner(n: i64) -> i64 {
        if n % 2 == 0 {
            n / 2
        } else {
            n * 3 + 1
        }
    }
    if n > 0 {
        inner(n)
    } else {
        0
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn classify_names_each_band() {
        assert_eq!(classify(-1), "negative");
        if classify(0) != "zero" {
            panic!("zero misnamed");
        }
        for n in [1, 2, 3] {
            assert_eq!(classify(n), "small");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn outer_folds_odd_and_even() {
        assert_eq!(outer(4), 2);
        assert_eq!(outer(-1), 0);
    }
}
